name: Deggendorf

sources.title: ZAW Donau-Wald – Mülltrennung (Restmüll, Papier, Bio)
sources.note: The operator's own separation guidance. Names exactly three household bins – Restmülltonne, Papiertonne, Biotonne – and lists what belongs in each. It states no container colours at all, so the lid_color half of every wheelie rule below is still uncorroborated.

sources.title: ZAW Donau-Wald – Was entsorgen? (waste-type directory)
sources.note: Per-material directory. Confirms glass is separated by colour (weiße / grüne / braune Glasflasche each have their own entry) and that Altkleider are collected separately.

sources.title: ZAW Donau-Wald – Kunststoffverpackungen
sources.note: CONTRADICTS the two packaging rules below. This operator routes plastic packaging to a Wertstoffinsel, not to a Gelber Sack or a Gelbe Tonne. See the verification notes.

sources.title: ZAW Donau-Wald – Altkleider
sources.note: Separate textile collection exists in this jurisdiction. The container form factor is not described.

sources.title: ZAW Donau-Wald – Wo entsorgen? (facility map)
sources.note: Facility types: Deponie, Recyclinghof, Wertstoffinsel, Grüngutannahmestelle. The Wertstoffinsel is the unit this pack's glass and packaging rules should be describing.

notes: DRAFT, and it must stay draft. Rules were transcribed from the predecessor project's four hard-coded classes plus general German practice – they are a starting point, not a verified source. Every source now carries a URL and a retrieval date, so RegionPack.is_publishable is true; that means the SOURCING bar is met and nothing more. `status` is the guard that keeps this away from users, and only a human who has checked the rules against the operator may move it.

VERIFICATION PASS, 2026-08-16, against the ZAW Donau-Wald sources listed above. Read this before trusting any rule here. Corroborated means the operator's own page says the stream exists and is collected separately; it does NOT mean the colour or the form factor in the `match` was confirmed. No source consulted states a single container colour, so the lid_color and body_color halves of every rule below remain unverified across the board.

CORROBORATED (stream exists, separately collected): deg-residual-wheelie – Restmülltonne is named explicitly. deg-paper-wheelie – Papiertonne is named explicitly. deg-bio-wheelie – Biotonne is named explicitly. deg-textiles – Altkleider have their own directory entry and a separate collection.

CONTRADICTED, and this is the important one: deg-packaging-sack and deg-packaging-wheelie. Both assert a kerbside packaging collection – a Gelber Sack at confidence 0.95 and a Gelbe Tonne at 0.88 – and the operator's own page for Kunststoffverpackungen routes packaging to a WERTSTOFFINSEL instead. Neither rule was corroborated and both are actively disputed by the source. They are left in place rather than deleted because removing a disposal rule is the maintainer's call and because ZAW Donau-Wald covers a whole district, so a yellow sack may still exist in some municipality within it – but on the evidence gathered here these two rules would tell a user in Deggendorf to use a container that is not collected. They must be resolved before this pack leaves draft.

UNCORROBORATED (plausible, no source found): the four igloo rules – deg-glass-igloo-generic, -clear, -green, -brown. The directory does confirm that glass is separated by colour (weiße, grüne and braune Glasflasche each have their own entry), so the three-way COLOUR SPLIT is real; what is unverified is that the container is an igloo and that its body colour indicates the glass colour. deg-street-basket – no source consulted covers street litter baskets, which are usually the municipality's rather than the waste authority's.

Deggendorf household setups observed by the original project: residual and paper bins next to houses, sometimes inside a locked shed; glass only at communal banks, typically near offices or larger buildings.

Glass banks are the known hard case. The predecessor's deck names Glas as 'the biggest problem'. Body colour alone is unreliable because many banks are a uniform green shell with per-aperture colour coding – hence requires_disambiguation on the generic rule until aperture detection lands in v2. The operator calls the unit a Wertstoffinsel, which is a SITE holding several containers rather than one container; a pack that models it as a single igloo is describing the wrong object, and that is worth settling before phase 6 tries to add a second city on top of this abstraction.
